title: First-party Instances omit the counterparty payment documents that third-party Instances must carry
content:
The six third-party Instances each carry two Active Data controllers: a List Of Distribution Reward Payments and a "Third Party Partner Payment Addresses And Transaction Records" document (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.1.2.3.3.5 and siblings), the latter holding the payee address and the per-payment transaction table.

The two first-party Instances — Sky.money App (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.1.2.1) and Sky.money Open Source Widgets (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.1.2.2) — carry only the first. There is no partner address document because there is no external partner to pay.

This is a small but informative departure from the Artifact's otherwise rigid uniformity. Elsewhere the structure is padded out even when empty: directories exist solely to declare that nothing can be added to them. Here a whole document is absent rather than present-and-empty, which signals that the counterparty record is genuinely inapplicable rather than merely unpopulated.

It also sharpens the earlier observation that Sky.money is funded as one Instance among many. It is on equal terms as far as attribution and reward accounting go — same primitive, same Reward Code slot, same payment list — but it is not at arm's length: rewards to a first-party surface produce no external transfer, so there is no transaction hash for an outside observer to check. The uniform treatment stops exactly where the money would leave the Agent.
description: The Sky.money App and Open Source Widgets Instances have no Third Party Partner Payment Addresses document, so the Instance schema flexes with whether an external payee exists.
